newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian Indian dies after being torched.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian Indian dies after being torched.

text.p: A Brazilian Indian who was soaked in a flammable liquid and set on fire by five youths on Sunday died of severe burn injuries on more than 90 percent of his body, a hospital spokeswoman said on Monday.

The spokeswoman said Galdino Jesus dos Santos, a 44-year-old Indian of the Pataxo tribe from the northeastern state of Bahia, had virtually no chance of surviving after he was rushed into a Brasilia hospital on Sunday morning.

Santos was set on fire while sleeping at a bus stop after he became separated from tribe members who had travelled with him to the Brazilian capital to take part in Saturday's Indian Day festivities. Police said he was set on fire by five upper-middle class youths, one of them the son of a federal judge, who were returning home after a night on the town.

"They were kids coming home from partying ... it was a teenage prank," a police officer said. The five youths were locked up in a separate cell after other inmates threatened to murder them, police said.
The murder of Santos caused widespread public outrage and President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said he was horrified by an act of such gratuitous barbarism.

Cristovan Buarque, the governor of the Federal District of Brasilia, declared three days of mourning in memory of Santos and called for harsh sentences for the culprits. "They deserve the toughest punishment the law permits," he told reporters.
